heading: INT. TAILOR'S ALTERATION ROOM, BACK OF A WEDDING SHOP - NIGHT

units.text: INT. TAILOR'S ALTERATION ROOM, BACK OF A WEDDING SHOP - NIGHT
A narrow room of mannequins and hanging gowns, pins scattered on the floor like silver rain.
A three-way mirror throws back endless versions of the same two women.

BEATRIX "BEA" LANDGRAF, sixties, tailor, kneels at the hem of a wedding dress with a mouthful of pins, while her client, SORAYA KHALILI, thirties, stands on the fitting platform in ivory silk, jaw tight, one hand clenched around a bouquet of paper flowers.
Bea tugs the hem and Soraya flinches.
Bea tugs again, harder, and Soraya looks down at her, and then past her to the three-way mirror where the dress looks like it belongs to someone happier.
Bea finally takes the pins from her mouth, sets them one by one in a velvet cushion, and stands, her knees cracking, while Soraya watches her in the glass instead of in person.
It's too long.
units.name: BEA

units.text: I know.
units.name: SORAYA

units.text: You told me three inches. It needs four.
units.name: BEA

units.text: Then four.
units.name: SORAYA

units.text: She said you'd say that.
units.name: BEA

units.text: Who said?
units.name: SORAYA

units.text: Your mother. She said you would let anyone cut anything.
units.name: BEA

units.text: Soraya turns her gaze to the floor.
Bea kneels again, takes a pin, and holds it up to the light.
She pushes it into the silk with a small deliberate click, and the dress seems to tighten around Soraya's ribs.
Bea. If I wanted to leave tonight -- through the back, through the alley -- would you stop me?
units.name: SORAYA

units.text: Bea doesn't answer.
She finishes the pin.
She reaches for another.

Then she sets her scissors on the cushion, stands, and, with both hands, begins unfastening the buttons down Soraya's spine, one by one by one, until the silk slides from her shoulders like a held breath.
The alley door sticks. Lift as you pull.
units.name: BEA
